corpus.properties: Flow-typed .js (~1,873 files under packages/). Parser behavior on this real-world dirty input is measured during each run and reconciled after both arm outputs are sealed; no solver may assume the retained v1 parser finding.

verificationCaveat: Version 2 retains judge-only evidence seeded 2026-08-02 on the pinned commit with ast-grep 0.45.0 and the local octocode build. Q8's function-count oracle is corrected from the retained v1 result evidence. Before scoring v2, verify the SHA, run both arms independently under the sealed-arm contract, and let an independent judge compare and reconcile the outputs. Parser degradation observed in v1 remains a measured historical finding, not a solver assumption.

harnessRules.note: Gotchas that produce false divergences — HARNESS errors, not tool findings. Apply before comparing counts.
rules: Line-number convention: ast-grep --json range.start.line is 0-BASED; octocode match lines are 1-BASED. Normalize (+1 on ast-grep) before diffing file:line sets.

File-set scope MUST be pinned: ast-grep '-l js' scans only .js; octocode structural with no include scans every supported extension (.ts test files too). Use include:["*.js"] on octocode — observed +8 phantom divergence in packages/react/src from one .ts test file.
Counting runs MUST lift octocode caps: maxFiles/itemsPerPage/maxMatchesPerFile well above the expected result size; verify stats.capReached is absent.
Metavar syntax: $X = one node, $$$X = list. octocode REJECTS $$X with a remediation message (2026-08-02+); ast-grep treats it as a never-matching literal.

octocode relative paths resolve against process cwd — always pass ABSOLUTE paths ($CORPUS/...). (A nonexistent path now errors loudly on every prefilter branch — fixed 2026-08-02; before that, literal-anchored patterns returned a silent 0.)

Flow parser recovery: v1 measured different behavior inside Flow-annotated regions. In v2, do not assume a direction or magnitude; inspect the sealed outputs and suspicious spans, then attribute any observed q3/q5 divergence.

Modifier semantics differ by design: octocode's bare `function $NAME(...)` does NOT match `async function` (explicit-modifier matching); ast-grep's does. Both match `export function` via the inner declaration node. Reconcile with explicit modifier patterns or a modifier-agnostic `kind: function_declaration` rule.
ast-grep 0.45 DOES ship yaml/json/markdown grammars AND an `outline` subcommand — never claim it lacks them; verify any grammar-gap claim at run time.
Time both arms per query (cold process) and record wall-clock as a guardrail; rerun any slow batch query solo before concluding failure.

q3.capabilityPoint: Sealed-arm fairness and judge-side reconciliation: each solver uses only its allowed primary arm, reports complete counts/anchors, and inspects suspicious spans; the independent judge attributes the normalized delta.
q3.expectedWorkflow: Each solver independently uses only its assigned structural-search arm, reports the complete normalized anchor set, and inspects suspicious returned spans. After sealing, the judge diffs both sets and reconciles the delta from those span records.

q6.expectedWorkflow: Use the assigned arm's strongest identity or per-hit verification capability, exclude the defining file and non-identity text hits, and aggregate the verified external references by file.
